# 11. Forms & Lead Capture

<!-- Generated by tools/build_checklists.py. Edit the generator to change checklist structure. -->

**Purpose:** Collect inquiries ethically and reliably on a static site using accessible forms and approved free-tier-friendly services only.

## Universal Constraints
- [ ] The solution must remain static front-end only: HTML, CSS, JavaScript, images, fonts, documents, and generated static files only.
- [ ] The stack must avoid proprietary lock-in, paid builders, paid plugins, closed hosting features that cannot be replaced, and opaque third-party scripts where an open or free-tier-friendly alternative exists.
- [ ] Every decision must be documented as a quality rule, acceptance criterion, or exception with rationale; implementation notes belong outside the checklist.
- [ ] Every checklist item must be testable by review, automated audit, source inspection, browser testing, or client sign-off.
- [ ] Manual exceptions must record the owner, reason, expiration date, affected pages, and residual risk.

## Must Exist
- [ ] A form inventory covering contact, quote, newsletter, booking, download, application, and feedback forms.
- [ ] A data minimization rule for every field and every hidden value.
- [ ] A form service decision record listing provider, free-tier limits, data location, retention, spam controls, export path, and deletion process.
- [ ] A no-backend fallback such as mailto link, phone link, downloadable brief, or alternate contact route.
- [ ] A consent model for marketing opt-in, privacy notice acknowledgement, and optional tracking.
- [ ] A validation standard for client-side validation, accessible error messages, required fields, and success messages.
- [ ] A spam prevention policy using non-invasive methods such as honeypot fields, rate limits from provider, or static-friendly CAPTCHA alternatives only when justified.
- [ ] A lead routing and response-time standard owned by the business.

## Must Be True
- [ ] Forms must use real labels associated with controls.
- [ ] Required fields must be visibly and programmatically identifiable.
- [ ] Users must know what happens after submission and how their data will be used.
- [ ] The form must not request sensitive personal data unless strictly necessary and legally approved.
- [ ] Form submissions must not expose personal data in query strings, public repositories, static JSON, analytics events, or URLs.
- [ ] Client-side validation must improve usability but must not be presented as secure server-side validation.
- [ ] Static form integrations must be replaceable and must allow data export or deletion.
- [ ] Newsletter signup must use explicit opt-in and must not be bundled with unrelated contact consent.

## Must Be Checked
- [ ] Check that every input has label, name, autocomplete where appropriate, type, help text if needed, and clear error state.
- [ ] Check that keyboard users can complete and submit the form.
- [ ] Check that success and error messages are announced to assistive technology.
- [ ] Check that the form action uses HTTPS and points to an approved provider or safe fallback.
- [ ] Check provider free-tier limits against expected lead volume and spam risk.
- [ ] Check that test submissions arrive, include required context, and exclude unnecessary tracking data.
- [ ] Check that privacy policy and consent copy match actual form behavior.
- [ ] Check that disabled submit states do not trap users without explanation.

## Must Be Avoided
- [ ] Avoid using paid-only form processors as a required dependency.
- [ ] Avoid placeholder form actions, broken thank-you pages, and silent failures.
- [ ] Avoid invisible consent, prechecked checkboxes, bundled marketing consent, and vague data-use language.
- [ ] Avoid CAPTCHA unless the spam risk justifies the accessibility and privacy cost.
- [ ] Avoid collecting files through static forms unless the provider and legal review explicitly support it.
- [ ] Avoid storing leads in email only when the business requires auditable follow-up.

## Premium Acceptance Standard
- [ ] Submitting a form must feel trustworthy, predictable, and recoverable.
- [ ] The site must offer at least one alternative contact path.
- [ ] Lead quality, privacy, accessibility, and reliability must outrank field volume.
- [ ] Every form must be tested on production, not only locally.

## Automation Hooks
- [ ] Use audits to flag missing labels, missing form actions, mailto-only forms, required fields without labels, and missing privacy links.
- [ ] Use generated templates only as starting points requiring legal and provider-specific review.

## Detailed Best-Practice Review Areas
- [ ] Form clarity: clear purpose, necessary fields only, visible labels, placeholders not replacing labels, required/optional fields, natural order, grouped long forms, short instructions, and specific submit buttons.
- [ ] Form trust: secure/professional feel, clear post-submit expectation, privacy expectations, polite specific errors, visible success/failure states, contact alternatives, spam protection without excessive friction, and mobile support.
- [ ] Form interaction: usable field sizes, correct input types, validation, errors near fields, preserved input, progress/confirmation states, disabled states, autofill, keyboard navigation, and no unnecessary complexity.
- [ ] Static form delivery: HTTPS production endpoint, correct recipient, test submissions received, thank-you/redirect behavior, consent language, privacy link, no private keys, no test endpoints, no console errors, and live-domain testing.
- [ ] Form tracking is privacy-safe: no field contents, names, emails, phones, messages, sensitive details, or successful-lead events before real success.

## Report Output Required
- [ ] Report every failed automated check with severity, checklist category, issue code, affected file or page, evidence, whether it is script-fixable, and how to fix it.
- [ ] Report every manual-only failure with reviewer, affected page or component, expected standard, actual behavior, recommended fix, owner, and target date.
- [ ] Separate launch blockers from quality improvements so critical static-site failures cannot be hidden by low-priority polish notes.
- [ ] Attach the JSON audit report, Markdown audit report, screenshots where visual proof is needed, and manual QA evidence for browser, device, keyboard, screen reader, form, analytics, and live deployment checks.

## Evidence Required
- [ ] Record reviewed pages, tools used, dates, reviewers, unresolved exceptions, and links to generated reports.
- [ ] Attach screenshots or source references for failures that cannot be proven by automated reports.
- [ ] Mark checklist items as complete only when the production static output satisfies the rule.
